# deadnix

Scan `.nix` files for dead code (unused variable bindings).

## Usage with Github Actions

See [deadnix-action](https://github.com/astro/deadnix-action)


## Usage with Nix Flakes

### Help

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- --help
Find dead code in .nix files

Usage: deadnix [OPTIONS] [FILE_PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [FILE_PATHS]...  .nix files, or directories with .nix files inside [default: .]

Options:
  -l, --no-lambda-arg                  Don't check lambda parameter arguments
  -L, --no-lambda-pattern-names        Don't check lambda attrset pattern names (don't break nixpkgs callPackage)
  -_, --no-underscore                  Don't check any bindings that start with a _
  -q, --quiet                          Don't print dead code report
  -e, --edit                           Remove unused code and write to source file
  -h, --hidden                         Recurse into hidden subdirectories and process hidden .*.nix files
      --help
  -f, --fail                           Exit with 1 if unused code has been found
  -o, --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>  Output format to use [default: human-readable] [possible values: human-readable, json]
      --exclude <EXCLUDES>...          Files to exclude from analysis
  -V, --version                        Print version
```

Reports contain ANSI color escape codes unless the
[`$NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org/) environment variable is set.

The `--exclude` parameter accepts multiple paths. Separate them with
`--` to pass `[FILE_PATHS]...`.

### Scan for unused code

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix example.nix
Warning: Unused declarations were found.
    ╭─[example.nix:1:1]
  1 │unusedArgs@{ unusedArg, usedArg, ... }:
    ·     │           ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg
    ·     ╰───────────────── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArgs
  3 │  inherit (builtins) unused_inherit;
    ·                            ╰─────── Unused let binding: unused_inherit
  5 │  unused = "fnord";
    ·     ╰─── Unused let binding: unused
 10 │  shadowed = 42;
    ·      ╰──── Unused let binding: shadowed
 11 │  _unused = unused: false;
    ·     │         ╰─── Unused lambda argument: unused
    ·     ╰───────────── Unused let binding: _unused
 13 │  x = { unusedArg2, x ? args.y, ... }@args: used1 + x;
    ·             ╰───── Unused lambda pattern: unusedArg2
```


### Remove unused code automatically

**Do commit** your changes into version control **before!**

```console
nix run github:astro/deadnix -- -eq test.nix
```

## Usage with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/)

Add the following to your project's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astro/deadnix
    rev: ID # frozen: VERSION
    hooks:
      - id: deadnix
        #args: [--edit] # Uncomment to automatically modify files
        stages: [commit]
```

Replace `ID` and `VERSION` above with the relevant version tag and
commit ID for reference, for example:

```yaml
rev: da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709  # frozen: v1.2.3
```

## Behavior

### Renaming of all unused to lambda args to start with `_`

If you disfavor marking them as unused, use option
`-l`/`--no-lambda-arg`.


### nixpkgs `callPackages` with multiple imports

`callPackages` guesses the packages to inject by the names of a
packages' lambda attrset pattern names. Some packages alias these with
`@args` to pass them to another `import ...nix args`.

As the used args are only named in the imported file they will be
recognized as dead in the package source file that is imported by
`callPackage`, rendering it unable to guess the dependencies to call
the packages with.

Use option `-L`/`--no-lambda-pattern-names` in this case.


### Skipping reports for certain declarations

As of 1.1.0 deadnix supports the following pragma to skip check of
bindings in the following line:

```nix
# deadnix: skip
```


## What if the produced reports are wrong?

Please open an issue. Do not forget to include the `.nix` code that
produces incorrect results.


## Commercial Support

The author can be hired to implement the features that you wish, or to
integrate this tool into your toolchain.

 "let a=1; in ''x ${a} y''\n",
 # paths

 "let a=1; in <a>\n",
 "let a=1; in /tmp/a\n",

 # identifiers with dash, quote, underscore
 "let a-b=1; in a-b\n",
 "let a-b=1; in a - b\n",
 "let a'=1; in a'\n",
 "let a_b-c'd=1; in 1\n",
 "let true=1; in true\n",
 "let false=1; null=2; in false\n",
 "let or=1; in or\n",
 "let rec=1; in rec\n",
 "true\n",
 "let a=true; in a\n",
 # keywords as attr names
 "{ let=1; in=2; }\n",
 "let a={let=1;}; in a.let\n",
 "let a={b=1;}; in a.b or 2\n",
]
for c in cases: js(c)

def run(args, cwd="/tmp/empty", env=None):

# This is clap 4 behavior. Implementing full clap error compatibility in Python is doable for common cases: help/version precedence seems based on order encountered? 
# Observations:
# --help --version => help (first special wins?)
# --version --help => version
# -hV => version ??? Wait -h is hidden flag in this app (hidden), not help! Important: -h is --hidden, help has no short. So -hV: hidden + version => version output.
# -Vh: version+hidden => version
# --help --bad => help, --bad --help => error (first token processed sequentially, help/version are early exit when encountered?)
# --version -o bad => version (early exit before validating later)
# What about invalid value before help: -o bad --help ?
for args in [["-o","bad","--help"],["-o","bad","--version"],["--bad","--version"],["-x","--help"],["--output-format","--help"],["-o"],["--help","-o"],["--version","-o"],["--help","--exclude"],["--exclude","a","--help"],["--exclude","a","--version"],["--exclude","--help"],["-l","--help","-l"],["-l","-l","--help"],["--help","-l","-l"],["-o=json","--bad"],["--bad","-o=json"]]:
    r=run(args); print(args, r.returncode, repr(r.stdout[:80]), repr(r.stderr[:250]))
# Full --help exact
r=run(["--help"]); print("HELP:\n"+r.stdout)
# args with equals for exclude multi: --exclude=a b ? b is positional.
for args in [["--exclude=a","b"],["--exclude","a","b"],["--exclude","a","--","b"],["--exclude","a","-l","b"],["-l","--exclude","a","b"],["b","--exclude","a"]]:
    r=run(args); print(args, r.returncode, repr(r.stdout[:100]), repr(r.stderr[:200]))

import subprocess, os

import subprocess, os
def js(content, extra=[]):
    open("/tmp/t/e.nix","w").write(content)
    e=dict(os.environ); e["NO_COLOR"]="1"
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+extra+["-o","json","e.nix"],cwd="/tmp/t",capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
    print(f"{content!r} -> {r.stdout.strip()!r}")
cases=[
 # inherit from expression scope in let
 "let x={b=1;}; inherit (x) b; in b\n", # x used by inherit-from if b live
 "let x={b=1;}; inherit (x) b; in 1\n", # b dead, x should be dead if user attributed to b
 "let inherit (y) b; y=1; in b\n", # y is sibling let binding used in from of b ; if from in scope, y used; style is weird let ordering irrelevant.
 "let y=1; inherit (y) b; in 1\n",
 "let inherit (x) b; in b\n", # x free
 # attrset inherit from scope: non-rec set inside a let: x as let binding
 "let x={b=1;}; in { inherit (x) b; }\n", # x used
 # rec set inherit from: can refer to rec attrs?
 "let z=1; in rec { x={b=1;}; inherit (x) b; y=b; }\n", # x is rec attr used in from...
 "rec { inherit (a) b; a=1; }\n", # a rec attr - not reportable
 # Assignment values dynamic keys scope

    r=subprocess.run([binp,"-o","json","e.nix"],cwd="/tmp/t",capture_output=True,env=e)
    return r.returncode, r.stdout, re.sub(rb"\(\d+\)",b"(PID)",r.stderr)

seeds=[
 "let a=1; b=2; in a + b\n",
 "{a, b ? 1, ...}@args: args.a\n",
 "let inherit (builtins) a b; in { x = a; y = [1 2.5 \"s ${a}\" ./foo]; }\n",
 "rec { a=1; b=a; c = if a then b else \"x\"; }\n",
 "with a; assert b; c: (d: d) 1\n",
 "let a=1; in a.b or (f a) ? c.d\n",
 "''ind ${a} ''$x'' + \"dq ${b} $$\"\n",
 "let a={x=1; \"y\"=2; ${z}=3; inherit q; inherit (w) r;}; in a\n",
]
random.seed(42)
tokens=["let","in","a","b","=",";","{","}","[","]","(",")",":",",",".","?","@","...","1","\"s\"","'","''","${","}","or","inherit","rec","if","then","else","with","assert","!","-","+","==","&&","//","++","<a>","./x","a:b","#c\n","/*c*/","é","$","~","`"]
fails=0; total=0
cases=[]
# mutations: delete/insert/replace random spans
for seed in seeds:
    for _ in range(200):
        s=seed
        for _ in range(random.randint(1,3)):
            op=random.choice(["del","ins","rep","dup"])
            if op=="ins":
                pos=random.randrange(len(s)+1); s=s[:pos]+random.choice(tokens)+s[pos:]
            elif len(s)>0:
                pos=random.randrange(len(s)); ch=random.choice(tokens)
                if op=="del": s=s[:pos]+s[pos+1:]
                elif op=="rep": s=s[:pos]+ch+s[pos+1:]
                else: s=s[:pos]+s[pos:pos+3]+s[pos:]
        cases.append(s)
# token soup
for _ in range(300):
    cases.append(" ".join(random.choice(tokens) for _ in range(random.randint(1,15)))+"\n")

import subprocess, os, random, re, shutil
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; MINE="/tmp/mybin/executable"
def run(binpath, content, extra, mode):
    d="/tmp/vf"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d); open(d+"/t.nix","w").write(content)
    e=dict(os.environ); e["NO_COLOR"]="1"
    args=extra+(["-e"] if mode=="edit" else [])+["t.nix"]
    r=subprocess.run([binpath]+args,cwd=d,capture_output=True,env=e)
    after=open(d+"/t.nix","rb").read()
    return r.returncode,r.stdout,re.sub(rb"\(\d+\)",b"(PID)",r.stderr),after

random.seed(7)
names=["a","b","c","x","y","_a","_b","foo","bar","a-b","unused1","used1"]
vals=["1","\"s\"","true","[ ]","{ }","1.5","./foo","a:b"]
def expr(depth, env):
    # env list of names in scope maybe
    choices=[]
    if env: choices+=["var"]*3
    choices+=["lit","app"]
    if depth<3: choices+=["let","lambda","pattern","set","recset","list","if","with","str","select"]
    k=random.choice(choices)
    if k=="var": return random.choice(env)
    if k=="lit": return random.choice(vals)
    if k=="let":
        ns=random.sample(names, random.randint(1,3))
        binds=" ".join(f"{n} = {expr(depth+1, env+ns)};" for n in ns)
        return f"(let {binds} in {expr(depth+1, env+ns)})"
    if k=="lambda":
        n=random.choice(names); return f"({n}: {expr(depth+1, env+[n])})"
    if k=="pattern":
        ns=random.sample(names, random.randint(1,3))
        entries=[]
        for n in ns:
            if random.random()<0.4: entries.append(f"{n} ? {expr(depth+1, env+ns)}")
            else: entries.append(n)
        at=random.choice(["", f"@{random.choice(names)}", f"{random.choice(names)}@"])
        # at syntax: either prefix name@ or suffix @name ; our fstring above for at uses at var weird; construct:
        if at.startswith("@"):
            pat=f"{{{', '.join(entries)}}}{at}"
        elif at.endswith("@") and at:
            pat=f"{at}{{{', '.join(entries)}}}"
        else:
            pat=f"{{{', '.join(entries)}}}"
        return f"({pat}: {expr(depth+1, env+ns)})"
    if k=="set":
        ns=random.sample(names, random.randint(0,3))
        return "{ "+" ".join(f"{n} = {expr(depth+1, env)};" for n in ns)+" }"
    if k=="recset":
        ns=random.sample(names, random.randint(1,2))
        return "rec { "+" ".join(f"{n} = {expr(depth+1, env)};" for n in ns)+" }"
    if k=="list": return "[ "+" ".join(expr(depth+1, env) for _ in range(random.randint(0,3)))+" ]"
    if k=="if": return f"(if {expr(depth+1,env)} then {expr(depth+1,env)} else {expr(depth+1,env)})"
    if k=="with": return f"(with {expr(depth+1,env)}; {expr(depth+1,env)})"
    if k=="str":
        v=random.choice(env) if env else "a"
        return "\"x ${"+v+"} y\""
    if k=="select":
        v=random.choice(env) if env else "a"
        return f"({v}.foo or {expr(depth+1,env)})"
    if k=="app":
        v=random.choice(env) if env else "f"
        return f"({v} {expr(depth+1,env)})"
    return "1"

# Example: skip hidden files and directories on unix

This uses the [`filter_entry`] iterator adapter to avoid yielding hidden files
and directories efficiently (i.e. without recursing into hidden directories):

```no_run
use walkdir::{DirEntry, WalkDir};
# use walkdir::Error;

fn is_hidden(entry: &DirEntry) -> bool {
    entry.file_name()
         .to_str()
         .map(|s| s.starts_with("."))
         .unwrap_or(false)
}

# fn try_main() -> Result<(), Error> {
let walker = WalkDir::new("foo").into_iter();
for entry in walker.filter_entry(|e| !is_hidden(e)) {
    println!("{}", entry?.path().display());
}
# Ok(())
# }
```
